ranking.note: Raised to P1: memory-amplification DoS resistance is the category's stated first priority, and the measured worst-case reduction (28 -> 1.6 bytes/WU) is larger in consequence than the bug fixes grouped at P2.
Raised to P2: unblocking fee-bumping of trimmed 1p1c parents is a pinning/censorship-resistance fix for package relay, on par with the other acceptance-correctness fixes at P2.
Lowered to P3: policy expansion revisiting a previously closed proposal with no cited downstream demand, unlike the concrete, evidenced P2 fixes.
Placed lower than its score position: most of its value is p2p/privacy; only the submitpackage 1p1c support falls inside this category.
Lowered to P4: the defect is unreachable on master and the motivation is the multiprocess IPC work, making it narrow and latent within mempool.

inconsistencies: #36328 and #36608 both change 1p1c package acceptance behaviour (reconsideration of trimmed package txs vs. adding package relay to submitpackage); review the focused #36328 first so the broader rewrite builds on settled semantics.

#36608's card claims it also fixes a fee-sum overflow with extreme prioritisetransaction deltas, which is the same defect #36367 addresses directly; #36367 is the targeted fix and should be reviewed first to avoid duplicated or divergent clamping logic.
#36895 explicitly depends on follow-up #36918 (not in this list) to recover the 50-70 ms/block validation regression; reviewers should treat them as a chain.
#36841 adds regression coverage for CVE-2025-62861, already fixed by merged #33504 - it is not duplicate work, but its value is purely preventive and should not be read as an open vulnerability.
#36214 and #36841 both add reorg-related mempool test coverage (cluster limits vs. TRUC/reorg invariants); they overlap in the reorg paths they exercise and are best reviewed together.
result.notes: The list splits cleanly: one DoS-resistance change with measured impact (P1), four evidenced acceptance/eviction correctness or policy fixes (P2), and a tail of test coverage, tooling and cross-category work (P3/P4). Several cards describe work whose centre of gravity is outside mempool (#35581 mining, #36608 p2p/privacy, #36880 init, #36816 IPC); they are ranked only on their mempool-visible effect.
